//productIdentityWorkflowNote: MOD-0033-FU02 §F.3 - nothing below is a secret, and nothing below switches the approval chain on. The switches (ProductIdentityWorkflow:Enabled, ProductIdentityWorkflowWorker:Enabled), the approver candidates and the service-client secret are written by scripts/dev/setup-service-trust.* to the git-ignored appsettings.Development.local.json, so a checkout that has not been bootstrapped behaves exactly as before.
//gskuWorkflowNote: WP-MDM-GSKU-ACCEPT-01 FIX1 (B6) - not secrets, and nothing here switches a flow on: the switches and approver candidates are written by scripts/dev/setup-service-trust.* to the git-ignored appsettings.Development.local.json. Each template code must exist as a published definition in Platform, and Platform's TrustedWorkflowStartAuthorization lists the same object type and code.
//lskuWorkflowNote: WP-MDM-LSKU-ACCEPT-01 FIX1 (B4) - as the GSKU note: not secrets, no switch. setup-service-trust.* writes the switches, the approver candidates and the two workers' Enabled to appsettings.Development.local.json; Platform's TrustedWorkflowStartAuthorization lists the same object types and codes.
//itemActivationWorkflowNote: MOD-0290-FU04 S2 - not secrets, and nothing here switches the flow on. Enabled and ApproverPositionId (the QA Manager position's id, from the owner's dev data) go to the git-ignored appsettings.Development.local.json by hand: the trust bootstrap (setup-service-trust.*) does not write this flow's section. The template code must exist as a published Platform definition, and Platform's TrustedWorkflowStartAuthorization lists {Diten.MDM, TRUSTED_WORKFLOW_CONSUMER, Item, ITEM-ACTIVATION}.
